text: {"headline":"Elevated 99215 use spread across all complexity tiers, including many low-complexity visits, but records came back for too few claims to confirm or rule out upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern raises concern: this provider's 99215 share runs several times the all-provider rate in every complexity tier, including patients with zero or one chronic condition, and 99214 dominates the overall mix. The sampled low-complexity 99215 claims carry simple diagnoses such as rash (R21), upper respiratory infection (J06.9), abdominal pain (R10.9) and follow-up (Z09), for example C0081131, C0082009 and C0082522. That is the pattern most consistent with upcoding rather than a sicker panel. Against that, the documentation is too thin to judge. Only one documented 99215 (C0082469, CKD, high MDM, 40 minutes) came back, and it supported the billed level. The documented 99213 and 99214 claims show no lopsided mismatch, and no notes claiming moderate-or-higher data reviewed lacked a lab or test line. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, especially the zero-condition R21, J06.9 and R10.9 visits, to see whether high-complexity MDM or time is actually documented."}
